description: How long to boil eggs, by size, starting temperature, altitude, and doneness. Times from the Williams heat-diffusion formula, for eggs lowered into boiling water.
intro: Boiling an egg looks simple until you want the same yolk twice. The time depends on the egg's weight, whether it came from the fridge or the counter, how high above sea level your stove sits, and how set you want the yolk. Change any one of those and the time moves by a minute or more.

Every calculator here uses the Williams formula, published by Charles D. H. Williams of the University of Exeter, which treats the egg as a sphere and works out when the edge of the yolk reaches the temperature you want. The egg weights are the USDA sizes, and the boiling points are the standard atmosphere figures for each altitude. Pick your egg, pick your yolk, and the time updates as you change the settings.

One thing to know before you start: every time assumes the egg goes into water that is already boiling. That is the method the formula describes, and it is the most repeatable way to boil an egg. The cold-start page covers the other method, eggs in cold water brought to the boil, with its own stand times from the American Egg Board.
metaDescription: How long to boil eggs? Exact times by egg size, fridge or room temp, altitude, and doneness, from the Williams formula. Soft, jammy, medium, and hard.
